clue.text: Cross after heading for beach to find litter

indicators.note: the cross is placed after the beach's first letter
the heading of a word is its first letter, so only the start of beach is used

parts.note: a rood is a cross or crucifix, especially in a church

explanation.surface: Someone on a beach tidy-up sets off with a cross to find rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'litter' looks like rubbish strewn on the sand, but it is the young animals born at one time.
explanation.definitionFit: A litter of kittens or puppies is a set of young born together, which is a brood.

clue.text: Malnourished patient possibly doctor's particular interest?

parts.note: one's bag is one's thing, as in not my bag
Bones is a nickname for a doctor, as in Star Trek or sawbones, so doctor's is of Bones

explanation.surface: A doctor is especially interested in a malnourished patient.
explanation.definitionFit: A very thin, underfed person is called a bag of bones, and a malnourished patient may be one.

clue.text: Horse wearing pair of spectacles? That's a surprise!

indicators.note: the horse has the spectacles on, so it sits inside them

parts.note: two round lenses look like the letters O O
H is slang for heroin, called horse

explanation.surface: A horse in glasses would be a surprise indeed.
explanation.definitionFit: Oho is an exclamation of surprise or triumph.

clue.text: Court case involves uplifting music

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting up turns the letters to read bottom to top
the case holds the courting word inside it

parts.note: a pod is a seed case
to court is to woo

explanation.surface: A court case features cheerful music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court case' looks like a lawsuit; it is two separate words.
explanation.definitionFit: Doo-wop is a style of vocal harmony pop from 1950s America, a kind of music.

clue.text: Apt to rise fast, perhaps, when crossing motorway

parts.note: tears or water well up, that is rise

indicators.note: the word for fast stretches across the motorway letter, holding it inside

parts.note: fast as in tied fast; tied is one way to be fast
M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: A driver seems inclined to speed up as they cross onto a motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: Something apt comes at the right moment, which is the sense of done at a good time.

clue.text: Stroke women's T-shirt so wantonly

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for women

indicators.note: acting wantonly is unrestrained, so the letters run wild

explanation.surface: Someone caresses a woman's T-shirt in a lewd way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stroke' suggests caressing; it is a hit in hockey.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrist shot is a hockey stroke played with a flick of the wrists.

clue.text: Still life's half mounted on print

indicators.note: in a down clue the half sits on top of the next piece
only the first half of the word for life is kept

parts.note: the word life, with the apostrophe s as a link
tho, short for though, means still or nevertheless

explanation.surface: A still-life painting is half mounted on a print.
explanation.definitionFit: A litho, short for lithograph, is a print made by lithography.

clue.text: Wake, taking hobnob for energy snack

parts.note: a wake is the trail left behind a boat
to hobnob is to mix socially

explanation.surface: At a funeral wake, someone grabs a Hobnob biscuit for energy.
explanation.walkthrough: A Hobnob is a popular British oat biscuit, but here hobnob is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Trail mix is a blend of nuts and dried fruit eaten by hikers for energy.

clue.text: I love 1AM ramble, after changing into jogging things?

indicators.note: the letters have been changed around, so they come out rearranged

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shown as O
1 is I, then A and M as written

explanation.surface: A jogger at one in the morning changes into running kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jogging' suggests running; it means jogging the memory.
explanation.definitionFit: Souvenirs and keepsakes trigger recollections, so they are things that jog the memory.

clue.text: As cellar, maybe, was sinking, last of beer removed

indicators.note: the final letter of beer is taken away from the drinking word

parts.note: sinking pints is drinking them, so was sinking is drank

indicators.note: takes the final letter of beer

explanation.surface: Someone in a cellar was downing beer until the last of it went.
explanation.definitionFit: A cellar is typically damp and cold, which is dank.

clue.text: Rock fan maybe after excitement googles it

indicators.note: letters that have been excited are stirred up, so the fodder is shuffled

explanation.surface: A music fan, worked up, searches the web for the band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock fan' suggests a lover of rock music; here it is someone keen on rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: A scientist who studies rocks could be called a rock fan, a playful example rather than a synonym.

clue.text: Athlete doing marathon initially wearing running things

indicators.note: applies to all three words before it, taking the opening letter of each

parts.note: to be in a coat is to be wearing it

explanation.surface: A marathon runner is pictured in their running kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running things' looks like jogging gear; it means managing affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Admin, short for administration, is the work of running an organisation's affairs.

clue.text: Station master in fact not moving posh car

indicators.note: letters that are moving shift about, so they are rearranged

parts.note: Roller is British slang for a Rolls-Royce

explanation.surface: A railway stationmaster, oddly, has a stationary luxury car.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fat Controller is the stout manager of the railway in the Thomas the Tank Engine children's stories.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Thomas the Tank Engine books, this character runs the railway and its stations, a station master of sorts.

clue.text: Sports officials are concerned with book

parts.note: matters that touch us concern us
Judges is a book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: Officials take an interest in a book.
explanation.walkthrough: Touch judges are the linesmen in rugby.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby, these officials patrol the touchlines and flag when the ball goes out.

clue.text: Members meeting at centre criticise poverty vocally

parts.note: to knock is to criticise

indicators.note: spoken aloud the word for poverty matches the second part

parts.note: need is poverty or want

explanation.surface: Members at a central meeting attack poverty in speeches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Members' suggests committee members; they are legs, which meet at the knees.
explanation.definitionFit: Being knock-kneed means one's legs, the limbs, curve in so the knees touch in the middle.

clue.text: Work, as non-drinkers do, after retirement

indicators.note: a retiring thing goes back, so the phrase is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: teetotallers sup nothing, that is SUP plus O for zero

explanation.surface: A teetotaller's habits after leaving work are described.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is read as SUP O, sup nothing, with O standing for zero.
explanation.definitionFit: An opus is a musical or literary composition, a work.

clue.text: Joyful exclamation: morning in bed devouring book that's trashy?

parts.note: whee! is a cry of delight

indicators.note: the lazy morning eats the book, taking it inside

parts.note: a lie-in is a morning spent in bed

explanation.surface: Someone happily spends a morning in bed reading a trashy novel.
explanation.walkthrough: A wheelie bin is the large wheeled rubbish bin used in British households.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheeled rubbish container is full of trash, a jokey take on something trashy.

clue.text: Stick up marquee perhaps to accommodate mass staging

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a cane is a walking stick

indicators.note: the tent houses the mass letter inside it

parts.note: a marquee is an example of a large tent
M is the symbol for mass

explanation.surface: Putting up a marquee for a large crowd at a show.
explanation.definitionFit: An enactment is a performance of a play or scene, so a staging of it.

clue.text: Contents of cask — raw lubricant — tipped over ramparts

indicators.note: tipped over turns the letters upside down, so they read from the bottom
the contents are letters found inside the run of words

explanation.surface: A barrel of crude oil is knocked over on castle walls.
explanation.definitionFit: Bulwarks are defensive walls or earthworks, synonymous with ramparts.

clue.text: CO perhaps to run out of things to say?

definitions.meaning: carbon monoxide is an example of the fumes from an engine

definitions.text: to run out of things to say?
definitions.meaning: to use up all one's chatter, gas being talk

explanation.definitionFit: Carbon monoxide is a fume an engine gives off, and humorously, using up all one's talk.

clue.text: Group to stop broadcasting

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard over the air, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: to block something is to stop it

explanation.surface: A group decides to stop a broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloc is a group of nations or parties allied for a common purpose.

clue.text: Person selling part of cooker with two rings missing

indicators.note: two O shapes are left out of the cooker part

parts.note: an oven door is part of a cooker
rings look like the letter O, so two rings are O O

explanation.surface: A salesman offers part of a cooker with two hob rings gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rings' suggests the hob's burners; they are O shapes.
explanation.definitionFit: A vendor is a seller, for example a street trader.

clue.text: Active early Liberal plugging slogan in support of wildlife sanctuary?

parts.note: a supporter's cry such as up with the workers

indicators.note: the Liberal fills a gap inside the sanctuary like a plug

parts.note: Noah's ark sheltered the animals from the flood

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician shouts a slogan backing a nature reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone up and about at dawn, when the lark sings, is active early.

clue.text: Bill and Al on reflection the pair to beat!

parts.note: a tab is a bill, as in pick up the tab

indicators.note: a reflection is a mirror image, so the name is read backwards

explanation.surface: Bill and Al, thinking it over, are the duo to defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the pair to beat' sounds like rivals; it is a pair of Indian hand drums.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabla is a pair of small Indian hand drums, played by beating them.

clue.text: Small round cuff

parts.note: a lap is a round of a track

explanation.surface: A short circular shirt cuff.
explanation.definitionFit: To cuff someone is to slap them with the open hand.

clue.text: Winter Olympian's weapon?

definitions.meaning: read as Winter Olympian is: a competitor who races a small sled feet first
the German semi-automatic pistol of that name

explanation.definitionFit: One who races the luge sled is so called, and a German pistol bears the same name.

clue.text: Poor condition of rhino and crocodile

parts.note: old British slang for money, as is bread
a crocodile is a line of schoolchildren walking in pairs, in British usage

explanation.surface: A rhinoceros and a crocodile are both in poor shape.
explanation.walkthrough: The animals are false leads: rhino is dated British slang for money, and a crocodile is a file of schoolchildren.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on the breadline is to live in poverty, the state of being poor.

clue.text: One's going to some trouble

definitions.meaning: I will, contracted, said by someone about to act

explanation.definitionFit: The contraction I'll means one is going to do something, and ill as a noun means harm.

clue.text: Offensive street drawings that could get you going!

parts.note: a push is a military offensive
drawings are art

explanation.surface: Rude street graffiti might provoke you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get you going' hints at provoking someone; it means getting a car moving.
explanation.definitionFit: Pushing a car to turn its engine over gets it moving, so a push-start gets you on your way.

clue.text: One left evidently indebted and annoyed

indicators.note: being evidently indebted is being plainly in the red, so the first pieces go in that colour

parts.note: to be in debt is to be in the red
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone left owing money is plainly upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Riled is an informal word for irritated or angered.
